akhfash:4-4.t: [He said] ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾: an exception falling outside the first part of the speech.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional; ﴿فاتَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); ﴿مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَآتُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ذَهَبَتْ أَزْواجُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِثْلَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «الله»; ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to «مؤمنون»; ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the clause is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the one addressed; ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿جاءَكَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْمُؤْمِناتُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿يُبايِعْنَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, the nūn being the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle that makes the verb accusative; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يُشْرِكْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the nūn being the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of a genitive governed by «على», and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وَلا يَسْرِقْنَ، وَلا يَزْنِينَ، وَلا يَقْتُلْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿أَوْلادَهُنَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَلا يَأْتِينَ﴾ conjoined to «أن يشركن»; ﴿بِبُهْتانٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿يَفْتَرِينَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, the nūn being the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed (muḍāf) to «أيديهن», and ﴿أَرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾ is conjoined to «أيديهن». ﴿وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ﴾ conjoined to «أن لا يشركن»; ﴿فِي مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَبايِعْهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it and, like it, has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ «إنّ», its noun and its two predicates, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿لا تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿غَضِبَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوما». ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); ﴿يَئِسُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿كَما يَئِسَ الْكُفَّارُ﴾ «كما»: both are attached to [a word that is] the naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْ أَصْحابِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْقُبُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, badal (substitute). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَدُوِّي﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to عدوي. ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿تُلْقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِالْمَوَدَّةِ﴾ both also attached to the verb.
﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿قَدْ كَفَرُوا﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿يُخْرِجُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الرَّسُولَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ conjoined to الرسول; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾ a badal from the Name of Majesty. ﴿أَنْ﴾ conditional. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿أَنْ﴾; the conditional particle in the Quranic text is ﴿إِنْ﴾.] ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun (ism). ﴿خَرَجْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the clause كنتم.. is initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿جِهاداً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿فِي سَبِيلِي﴾ both attached to جهادا. ﴿وَابْتِغاءَ﴾ conjoined to جهادا. ﴿مَرْضاتِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تُسِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿بِالْمَوَدَّةِ﴾ both also attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿أَنَا أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to أعلم. ﴿أَخْفَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَما أَعْلَنْتُمْ﴾ conjoined to ما أخفيتم. ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْهُ﴾ a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ, and an imperfect verb, jussive, and the hāʾ is its object, the fāʿil being latent. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification. ﴿ضَلَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿سَواءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to السبيل. ﴿السَّبِيلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the verbal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause من.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿إِنْ يَثْقَفُوكُمْ﴾ إن is conditional, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its noun (ism); the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿أَعْداءً﴾ the khabar of يكونوا. ﴿وَيَبْسُطُوا﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to يكونوا. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَلْسِنَتَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أيديهم. ﴿بِالسُّوءِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَوَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ لو is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from لو and what follows it is the object of ودوا.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن, and its object. ﴿أَرْحامُكُمْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَلا أَوْلادُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to أرحامكم. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَفْصِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) بصير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿قَدْ كانَتْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq) and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان. ﴿أُسْوَةٌ﴾ its postponed noun (ism). ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of أسوة; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أسوة. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to إبراهيم. ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from إبراهيم. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِقَوْمِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّا بُرَآؤُا﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to برآء.
﴿وَمِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ both conjoined to منكم, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَفَرْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَبَدا بَيْنَنا﴾ a past verb and an adverb of place, and ﴿بَيْنَكُمُ﴾ is conjoined to بيننا. ﴿الْعَداوَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَالْبَغْضاءُ﴾ conjoined to العداوة. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive. ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after حتى. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَحْدَهُ﴾ ḥāl; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بدا. ﴿إِلَّا قَوْلَ﴾ a particle of exception and the excepted, accusative. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِأَبِيهِ﴾ both attached to قول. ﴿لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لَكَ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both also attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أملك. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to توكلنا; the vocative clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿تَوَكَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَإِلَيْكَ﴾ both attached to what follows them. ﴿أَنَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِلَيْكَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿لا تَجْعَلْنا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and ﴿نا﴾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) فتنة; the vocative and verbal clauses are both resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَاغْفِرْ﴾ a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), and ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) of what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ two khabars (predicates); the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), and the verbal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كانَ لَكُمْ﴾ kāna, and a preposition and its genitive noun as its fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar. ﴿أُسْوَةٌ﴾ the postponed noun (ism) of كان. ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is the response to the implied oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from لكم. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir). ﴿يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the Name of Majesty is its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of كان, and the clause كان.. is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَالْيَوْمَ﴾ conjoined to الله. ﴿الْآخِرَ﴾ a ṣifa. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَتَوَلَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ﴾ two khabars; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clause من.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ﴾ ʿasā and its noun (ism), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is the khabar (predicate) of عسى, and the clause عسى is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined to بينكم. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عادَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَوَدَّةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَاللَّهُ قَدِيرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُمْ﴾ conjoined to لم يقاتلوكم, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الذين. ﴿وَتُقْسِطُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿يُحِبُّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:9-9.t:
﴿إِنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and an imperfect verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنِ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قاتَلُوكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي الدِّينِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).
﴿أَخْرَجُوكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ظاهَرُوا عَلى إِخْراجِكُمْ﴾ also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الذين. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَتَوَلَّهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause من..
is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاءَكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and ﴿الْمُؤْمِناتُ﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مُهاجِراتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿بِإِيمانِهِنَّ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the nominal clause is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿إن﴾ conditional. ﴿عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُؤْمِناتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is connective, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object. ﴿إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿هُنَّ حِلٌّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to حل; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحِلُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾ both attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿آتُوهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its first object. ﴿ما﴾ its second object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿جُناحَ﴾ its noun (ism), indeclinable on fatḥa. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿إِذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾ إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of time, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ its second object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلا تُمْسِكُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِعِصَمِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْكَوافِرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَسْئَلُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْفَقْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلْيَسْئَلُوا﴾ a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command (lām al-amr), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. And ﴿ذلِكُمْ حُكْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ with ḍamma; as muḍāf ilayhi the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهِ﴾.] The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَحْكُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذَا جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتُ مُهَاجِرَاتٍ فَٱمْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾.
It means: make them swear an oath. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ made peace with the people of Mecca at al-Ḥudaybiya, and the document had been sealed, Subayʿa bint al-Ḥārith al-Aslamiyya came out to him as a Muslim. Her husband came and said: Return her to me, for that is in the condition we have against you, and this is the clay of the writing, not yet dry. So this verse came down: ﴿فَلاَ تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ لاَ هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَّهُمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ﴾.
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made her swear: that nothing brought you out to us except eagerness for Islam and desire for it, and that no misdeed you committed brought you out, nor hatred of your husband. She swore, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave her husband her dowry, and the revelation came down: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُواْ بِعِصَمِ ٱلْكَوَافِرِ﴾.
Whoever had a wife in Mecca who refused to become Muslim, the marriage bond (ʿiṣma) between her and her husband was cut; and whichever of their women came out to the Muslims as a Muslim, her bond with her unbelieving husband was cut, and the Muslims may marry her without a waiting period (ʿidda).
His saying: ﴿وَاسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقْتُمْ وَلْيَسْأَلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْ﴾.
He is saying: ask the people of Mecca to return to you the dowries of the women who go out from you to them as apostates, and let them ask for the dowries of those of their women who come out to you.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُمْسِكُواْ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it without doubling [تُمْسِكوا], and al-Ḥasan read it: تُمسّكوا; the meaning is close.
The Arabs say: أمسكت بك, مسكت بك and تمسّكت بك (I held fast to you).

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ شَيْءٌ﴾: [i.e.] escaped you. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وإن فاتكم أحد من أزواجكم". أحد is valid in the place of شىء, and شىء is valid in the place of أحد when it refers to people; but when شىء refers to something other than people, أحد is not valid in its place.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن فَاتَكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: [if one] escapes you — if a woman goes off and joins the people of Mecca as an unbeliever, and there is no covenant between you and them — and then you ﴿فَعَاقَبْتُمْ﴾, he is saying: you took booty, then give her husband her dowry from the booty before the fifth (khums) [is taken].
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, that he read "فعاقبتم" and explained it as: you took booty. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it: فعقّبتم, with doubling; it is like your saying تصعّر and تصاعر, among words of which I have informed you concerning the kinship of [the patterns] faʿʿaltu and fāʿaltu.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلاَدَهُنَّ﴾.
Al-Sulamī alone read it: ولا يقتّلن أولادهن. It is mentioned that when the Prophet ﷺ conquered Mecca he sat on al-Ṣafā with ʿUmar beside him, and the women came to him to give their pledge; among them was the daughter of ʿUtba [i.e. Hind]. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿لاَّ يُشْرِكْنَ بِٱللَّهِ شَيْئاً﴾ — he was saying: do not worship idols, do not steal and do not commit fornication — Hind said: And does a free woman commit fornication? He said: ʿUmar laughed, then said: No, by my life, a free woman does not commit fornication. He said: And when he said: Do not kill your children — this concerned the burying alive that the people of the Jāhiliyya used to practise, and they pledged not to do it — Hind said: We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتَٰنٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَأَرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾.
A woman would pick up a foundling and say to her husband: This is my child by you. That is the fabricated slander (buhtān) [198/a].

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَتَوَلَّوْاْ قوْماً غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ قَدْ يَئِسُواْ مِنَ ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
He is saying: [they have despaired] of the bliss of the Hereafter and its reward, just as the unbelievers have despaired of the people of the graves. He is saying: they [the dead unbelievers] know that there is no bliss for them in this world, since they have died and entered the graves.
And it is also said: just as the unbelievers who are among the people of the graves have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter and its bliss.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it: يُفصِّل بينكم; he [al-Farrāʾ] said: and Abū Zakariyyā [i.e. al-Farrāʾ himself] reads it the same way. ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan read it: يَفْصل, and the people of Medina read it: يُفْصَل.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ﴾. He means Ḥāṭib; "فيهم" means: in Abraham. He is saying: in what Abraham and those with him did when they declared themselves free of their people. He is saying: Why did you not take Abraham as your example, O Ḥāṭib, and declare yourself free of your family as Abraham declared himself free? Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لأَبِيهِ﴾, that is: you had an example in their deeds except in Abraham's saying "I will surely ask forgiveness [for you]", for in that you have no example.
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا بُرَءآؤاْ مِّنْكُمْ﴾. If you drop the hamza of برآء, you point to it with your chest and say: بُرَاء. Al-Farrāʾ said: [it is] a lengthening and a pointing toward the hamza, and it can only be captured precisely by hearing, [and he did not make it fully declinable (lam yujrihā)]. Some of the Arabs say: إِنا بِراءٌ منكم, making it fully declinable (yujrī); had it been read that way it would be a valid reading.
His saying: ﴿رَّبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا﴾. That is: so say this saying yourselves; and it is also said that it is part of what Abraham, peace be upon him, and his people said.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا لاَ تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً﴾. [Meaning:] Do not let the unbelievers prevail over us, so that they would think that they are in the right and that we are in falsehood.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيْتُم مِّنْهُم مَّوَدَّةً﴾.
He is saying: perhaps the enmity between you will turn back into affection. Then the Prophet ﷺ married Umm Ḥabība, daughter of Abū Sufyān, and the marriage tie became affection.

farraa:8-9.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَنْهَاكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
These are Khuzāʿa: they had made a pact with the Prophet ﷺ that they would not [197/b] fight him and would not drive him out, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered that they be treated kindly and that the pact with them be kept until the end of its term. Then He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَنْهَاكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَاتَلُوكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخْرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ وَظَاهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ إِخْرَاجِكُمْ أَن تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾: [that is,] that you support them; meaning the rest of the people of Mecca.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِٱلْمَوَدَّةِ﴾.
The entry of the bāʾ in «المودة» and its omission are the same. This is like your saying: «أظن أنك قائم» and «أظن بأنك قائم» (I think that you are standing), and «أريد بأن تذهب», «أريد بأن تقوم» (I want you to go / to stand). Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has said: ﴿ومَنْ يُرِدْ فيه بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾, inserting the bāʾ, while the meaning is: «ومن يرد فيه إلحادا» (whoever intends deviation in it).
Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
فلمّا رجتْ بالشُّرب هزَّلها العصا * شحيحٌ لهُ عند الإزاءِ نهيمُ
(When she hoped to drink, a niggardly man shook the stick at her, growling at the trough's mouth.)
Its meaning is: when she hoped that she would drink.
This sura was revealed about Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to attack the people of Mecca, a woman from the clients of Banū al-Muṭṭalib came to him, and the Muslims gave her gifts. When she wanted to return, Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa came to her and said: "I will give you ten dinars and clothe you with a cloak, on condition that you deliver a letter to the people of Mecca." So he wrote (a letter) with her, and she set off making for Mecca. Gabriel came down to the Prophet ﷺ (lit. may Allah bless them both) with the news, and he sent ʿAlī and al-Zubayr after her, saying: "If she hands the letter over to you, (well); [otherwise strike] [197/ا] her neck." They caught up with her, and she said: "Stand away from me, for I know that you will not believe me until you search me." He said: she took the letter and put it between two of her braids. They searched her and saw nothing, and turned back. Then ʿAlī said to al-Zubayr: "What have we done? The Messenger of Allah tells us that she has a letter, and we believe her?" So they turned back on her and said: "You will bring out your letter, or we will strike your neck." When she saw they were in earnest, she brought out the letter.
In it was: "From Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa to the people of Mecca. To proceed: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intends to attack you, so take your precautions," along with other things he wrote. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Ḥāṭib, and he admitted it to him and said: "What led me to this is that my family is in Mecca, and there is not [one] of your companions who does not have someone in Mecca to defend his family; so I wanted to gain favour with them so that they would look after my dependants. And I knew that my letter would not benefit them, and that Allah would carry out His command upon them." ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "Let me strike his neck." He said: the Prophet ﷺ was silent, then said: "What do you know? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you."
Al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥibbān told me this with his chain of transmission.
And His saying: ﴿تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِٱلْمَوَدَّةِ﴾: it is part of the ṣila (qualifying clause) of «الأولياء», as in your saying: «لا تتخذنّه رجلا تلقى إليه كلّ ما عندك» (do not take him as a man to whom you divulge everything you have).
And His saying: ﴿يُخْرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَن تُؤْمِنُواْ﴾: (i.e.) «إن آمنتم» (if you believe) and «لإن آمنتم» (because you believe). Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهَاداً فِي سَبِيلِي﴾, then do not take them as allies.
«[Translator's note: «لإن» is as printed, presumably for «لأن» (because).]»

zajjaj:2-2.t: Then Allah the Exalted informed them that seeking closeness to them by passing on the reports of the Prophet ﷺ would not benefit them, and He said: ﴿إنْ يَثْقَفُوكم يَكُونُوا لَكم أعْداءً﴾. The meaning of ”يَثْقَفُوكُمْ“ is: they meet you (find you). ﴿وَيَبْسُطُوا إلَيْكم أيْدِيَهم وألْسِنَتَهم بِالسُّوءِ﴾.

zajjaj:3-3.t: Then He informed them that their kin and their children will not benefit them at all on the Day of Resurrection, and He said: ﴿لَنْ تَنْفَعَكم أرْحامُكم ولا أوْلادُكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾. ”يَفْصِلُ“ has been read in four ways: ”يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, in the sense of "Allah will judge between you"; ”يُفْصَلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), the meaning referring back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; ”يُفَصَّلَ بَيْنَكُمْ“, with a doubled ṣād carrying a fatḥa and a ḍamma on the yāʾ, again as a verb whose agent is not named; and it was read ”يُفَصِّلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“. It is also permissible to say ”نُفَصِّلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“ and ”نَفْصِلُ بَيْنَكُمْ“, with nūn. So these are six ways.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قَدْ كانَتْ لَكم أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ﴾ — it is also permissible to say ”أُسْوَةٌ“ with a ḍamma on the hamza [Translator's note: the word as printed already carries a ḍamma; the intended contrast is presumably with the kasra form إسْوة] — ﴿فِي إبْراهِيمَ والَّذِينَ مَعَهُ إذْ قالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إنّا بُرَآءُ مِنكم ومِمّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the companions of Ibrāhīm — Allah's blessings be upon him — disowned their people and showed them enmity, and He commanded the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ to take them, and their words, as an example.

His saying: ﴿إلا قَوْلَ إبْراهِيمَ لأبِيهِ لأسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ﴾ — that was only because of a promise he had made him; then when it became clear to him that he persisted in disbelief, he disowned him. As for what is permissible in ”بُرَءاءُ مِنكُمْ“, there are four ways. The best of them is ”بُرَءاءُ“ on the pattern ”فُعَلاءُ“, like ”ظَرِيفٌ“ / ”ظُرَفاءُ“ and ”شَرِيكٌ“ / ”شُرَكاءُ“; likewise ”بَرِيءٌ“ / ”بُرَءاءُ“. It is also permissible to say ”بُراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ and ”بَراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ [Translator's note: the third form, discussed next, is printed here as بَراء, while the explanation that follows is of بِراء with kasra], both with madd (a long vowel). Whoever says ”بِراءٌ“ with madd treats it like ”ظَرِيفٌ“ / ”ظِرافٌ“; and whoever says ”بُراءٌ“ with ḍamma has substituted the ḍamma for the kasra, just as they said ”رُخْلَةٌ“ / ”رِخالٌ“, and some of them said ”رُخالٌ“ with a ḍamma on the rāʾ; and they said ”شاةٌ رُبًّى“ (a recently-delivered ewe), with ”غَنَمٌ رُبابٌ“ and ”رِبابٌ“, with ḍamma and kasra on the rāʾ — that is, the one that has recently given birth, i.e. recently delivered. It is also permissible to say ”بَراءٌ مِنكُمْ“ with a fatḥa on the bāʾ, because the Arabs say ”أنا البَراءُ مِنكَ“ (I am quit of you), and two or three people say ”نَحْنُ البَراءُ مِنكَ“, and likewise a woman says ”أنا البَراءُ مِنكَ“. But do not recite any of these ways except what has been recited by someone from whom the reading is transmitted.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ — its meaning is: do not give them victory over us, so that they think they are in the right and are thereby led astray (yuftatanū).

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿عَسى اللَّهُ أنْ يَجْعَلَ بَيْنَكم وبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ عادَيْتُمْ مِنهم مَوَدَّةً﴾ — ”عَسى“ from Allah is binding (certain). It has come in the exegesis that by this He means that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umm Ḥabība, daughter of Abū Sufyān, and that this is the affection. It is also said that He means by it those of them who embraced Islam, so that there would be affection between you and them.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿لا يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقاتِلُوكم في الدِّينِ ولَمْ يُخْرِجُوكم مِن دِيارِكم أنْ تَبَرُّوهُمْ﴾ — ”أنْ“ is in the position of the genitive, a badal (substitute) for ”اَلَّذِينَ“. The meaning is: "He does not forbid you from being kind to those who did not fight you on account of religion." This indicates that the meaning is: "Allah does not forbid you from being kind to those between whom and you there is a covenant," and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَتُقْسِطُوا إلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. and that you act justly in what is between you and them, by fulfilling the covenant. One says ”أقْسَطَ الرَّجُلُ، فَهو مُقْسِطٌ“ when he acts justly, and ”قَسَطَ، فَهو قاسِطٌ“ when he acts unjustly. It is also said that He means by it women and children.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّما يَنْهاكُمُ اللَّهُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ قاتَلُوكم في الدِّينِ وأخْرَجُوكم مِن دِيارِكم وظاهَرُوا عَلى إخْراجِكم أنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾ — ”ظاهَرُوا عَلى إخْراجِكُمْ“ means: they helped one another in expelling you. ﴿أنْ تَوَلَّوْهُمْ﴾: ”أنْ“ is also in the position of the genitive, as a badal (substitute). The meaning is: "Allah only forbids you from taking as allies these who fought you on account of religion," because writing to them by disclosing what the Prophet ﷺ had kept secret is alliance (muwālāt).

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا جاءَكُمُ المُؤْمِناتُ مُهاجِراتٍ﴾ — the position of ”مُهاجِراتٍ“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). They were called ”اَلْمُؤْمِناتُ“ (the believing women) even though they were not known for faith and before they reached the Prophet ﷺ; they were only named so because faith was presumed of them. ﴿فامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ﴾ means: test them. This was revealed because of the covenant of al-Ḥudaybiya which was between the Prophet ﷺ and those in Makka who made a covenant with him, of Khuzāʿa and others. He ﷺ had made a covenant with them that whoever came to him from them he would return to them, and whoever went over to them from him they would not return to him. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that whoever of the believing women came, of those who wished to enter Islam, were not to be returned to the disbelievers; that is His saying: ﴿فامْتَحِنُوهُنَّ اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِإيمانِهِنَّ﴾. So He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that outward profession of faith comes within the scope of Islam, while Allah knows what is in the hearts. The test, when an emigrant woman came, was that she be made to swear by Allah that it was not resentment against her husband that brought her, and that she came only out of love for Allah and His Messenger and out of desire for Islam; this was the test. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَلا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إلى الكُفّارِ﴾ means: do not send them back. One says ”رَجَعَ فُلانٌ“ (so-and-so returned) and ”رَجَعْتُهُ“ (I returned him).

His saying: ﴿لا هُنَّ حِلٌّ لَهم ولا هم يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّ﴾ means: the believing women are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women. ﴿وَآتُوهم ما أنْفَقُوا﴾ — the husband used to be given the dowry of his wife who had believed, and the dowry used to be taken from them for whichever of the believers' wives went over to them, of those who joined her husband when she inclined to disbelief and persisted in it. ﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ means: there is no sin upon you ﴿أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾, i.e. in marrying them, ﴿إذا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾; this is evidence that marriage must include a dowry. ﴿وَلا تُمْسِكُوا بِعِصَمِ الكَوافِرِ﴾ means: when they disbelieve, the tie (ʿiṣma) between the polytheist woman and the believer has ceased, i.e. the knot of the rope of marriage has been severed. The root meaning of ”اَلْعِصْمَةُ“ is a rope, and whatever holds something has "held fast" (ʿaṣama) it. It was read ”وَلا تُمْسِكُوا“ and ”وَلا تَمَسَّكُوا“, the original being ”تَتَمَسَّكُوا“, from your saying ”تَمَسَّكْتُ بِالشَّيْءِ“ (I held on to the thing), when you do not let it go from your hand or your will; one of the two tāʾs was elided. It was read ”تُمَسَّكُوا“ with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and doubling, from your saying ”مَسَّكَ، يُمَسِّكُ“ [Translator's note: the vowelling تُمَسَّكُوا as printed has a fatḥa on the sīn; the form derived from مَسَّكَ يُمَسِّكُ would be تُمَسِّكُوا]; and it was read ”تُمْسِكُوا“ with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and the sīn undoubled, in the sense of ”أمْسَكَ، يُمْسِكُ“.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ فاتَكم شَيْءٌ مِن أزْواجِكم إلى الكُفّارِ فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ — on the pattern ”فاعَلْتُمْ“. It was also read ”فَعَقَبْتُمْ“, without alif and with an undoubled qāf. It has come in the exegesis: "and you took spoils." Its interpretation in the language is: "the outcome (al-ʿuqbā) was yours," i.e. "the outcome and the victory were yours, so that you took spoils." ”عَقِبْتُمْ“ [Translator's note: so printed; the context, which speaks next of the undoubled form and then says the doubled form is more emphatic, suggests the doubled form عَقَّبْتُم was intended] is the best of them in the language, and ”فَعَقَبْتُمْ“ without doubling is also good in the language, i.e. "the outcome of victory became yours," except that with doubling it is more emphatic. The meaning of ﴿فَعاقَبْتُمْ﴾ is: you struck them in battle with a punishment until you took spoils; i.e. if a woman of yours went off to those between whom and you there is no covenant, ﴿فَآتُوا الَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتْ أزْواجُهم مِثْلَ ما أنْفَقُوا﴾, i.e. the like of what they spent on their dowries. Likewise if she went off to those between whom and you there is a covenant and they broke faith in paying the dowry: the one whose wife had gone used to be given the dowry from the spoils, so that nothing of his right was diminished; he was given his right in full after the women's dowries were taken out. It is for this reason that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may Allah have mercy on him — paid, according to what they have related, the dowry of Umm Ayman.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا جاءَكَ المُؤْمِناتُ يُبايِعْنَكَ عَلى أنْ لا يُشْرِكْنَ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا ولا يَسْرِقْنَ ولا يَزْنِينَ ولا يَقْتُلْنَ أوْلادَهُنَّ ولا يَأْتِينَ بِبُهْتانٍ يَفْتَرِينَهُ بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِنَّ وأرْجُلِهِنَّ﴾ means: they will not bring a child which they attribute to the husband, for that is a slander and a fabrication. ﴿وَلا يَعْصِينَكَ في مَعْرُوفٍ﴾ — it is said: they will not disobey you in a matter concerning wailing (over the dead); and it is said: in tearing clothes, scratching faces and conversing with men. The sum of it is that the meaning is: "they will not disobey you in anything you command them that is right."

It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ sat on al-Ṣafā, and ʿUmar — may Allah have mercy on him — sat below him, and they would pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ on what the verse contains, and wipe their hands on the hand of ʿUmar. And it is said: "they used to wipe with their hands from behind a garment."»

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الآخِرَةِ﴾ — He means by it the Jews. ﴿كَما يَئِسَ الكُفّارُ مِن أصْحابِ القُبُورِ﴾ means: just as the disbelievers who do not believe with certainty in the resurrection have despaired of their dead being raised, so the Jews and those who made a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ have despaired of having any share in the Hereafter. And it is said: ﴿قَدْ يَئِسُوا مِنَ الآخِرَةِ كَما يَئِسَ الكُفّارُ مِن أصْحابِ القُبُورِ﴾ means: of those who are in the graves; they know that they have no share in the Hereafter. [Translator's note: i.e. on this view the despairing disbelievers are themselves the people of the graves.]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mumtaḥana
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكم أوْلِياءَ تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ﴾ — it has been said that the meaning is: "تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمُ المَوَدَّةَ" (you offer them affection) [Translator's note: i.e. with the bāʾ redundant]. But the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "they convey to them the news of the Prophet, upon him be peace, and his secret, by reason of the affection that is between you and them". The evidence for this view is ﴿تُسِرُّونَ إلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Mumtaḥana: 1]: (you secretly pass on to them) what the Prophet, upon him be peace, keeps hidden, out of affection. It is transmitted «that it was revealed concerning Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. He had written to the people of Mecca, professing sincere counsel to them, and wrote to them: "The Messenger of Allah intends to campaign against you, so take your precautions." Allah informed His Prophet of that. He had written them a letter and sent it with a woman who, it is said, was a client (mawlāt) of the Banū Hāshim. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent ʿAlī and al-Zubayr after her. They caught up with her and asked her about the letter, but she denied it. They searched what she had with her and found nothing. Then ʿAlī, may Allah's good pleasure be upon him, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not told us a lie", and ʿAlī swore to her that she would bring out the letter or he would strike her with the sword. She said to them: "Turn your faces away", and brought out the letter from one of the plaits of her hair. He brought the letter to the Prophet, upon him be peace, who showed it to Ḥāṭib; he admitted it and said: "I have family and property in Mecca, so I wanted to gain favour with them; and Allah will not turn His might away from them." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾ (the verse), to the end of the account.»
As for His saying: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهادًا في سَبِيلِي وابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي﴾ — this is a condition (sharṭ) whose answer (jawāb al-sharṭ, apodosis) has come before it; the meaning is: "if you have gone out striving in My way and seeking My good pleasure, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies". "جِهادًا" and "اِبْتِغاءَ" are both accusative (manṣūb) because they are mafʿūl lahu (objects of purpose); the meaning is: "if you have gone out for striving and seeking My good pleasure, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies."
